answer: Decentralized networks resist Sybil attacks by requiring bonded stakes and graph cut verification: isolated identity clusters fail topological cuts because suspicious subgraphs cannot fake high min-cut connectivity. Auditing agents act like the falcon hunting fraudulent nodes, slashing pledged deposits to make attacks impose exponential cost. The fable of effortless consensus falls apart as honest nodes reap network nectar while fraudulent duplicates face total stake loss.
